scores.evidence: Strengths verified: the four skills (skills/SOURCES.md 153 lines, SYNTHESIS.md, TRANSLATION.md, TRANSCRIPTS.md) are precise, numbered, carry worked examples and ordered self-checks, and state failure modes explicitly (TRANSLATION.md section 3). Each skill-backed agent (.claude/agents/extract.md, fidelity-check.md, synthesize.md, render.md) injects its skill verbatim between BEGIN/END markers, and tests/test_agents.py enforces byte-equality. Tool least-privilege is real and not just frontmatter: every agent is `tools: Read, Write`; pipeline/agents.py build_command passes --tools, path-scoped --allowedTools, deny rules for read-only dirs, protected records and any answer_key.json, --setting-sources project,local from a neutral cwd, --strict-mcp-config and --permission-prompts none. Rule U (untrusted content) is present in every runtime prompt and pinned by tests/test_prompt_hygiene.py, which also blocks graded-fixture n-grams and seeded strings; at HEAD the runtime prompts are decontaminated (grep for ογδόντα/μπραντ/Meltemi/hold me in skills/ and .claude/agents/ returns nothing). Many rules have gates that cite them: classify rule 3 (stages.py check_classification), TRANSCRIPTS section 4 escalation and byte-exact annotation (check_fidelity), SYNTHESIS rules 1, 4, 5, 7 and 8 (check_synthesis: anchor sweep, resolution-by-omission, same-speaker retraction, currency trace, no readiness), and verifier evidence screening (extraction.py screen_findings). The verifier's findings go through an adjudication order, not blind obedience (build_verified_repair_order). Weaknesses: (1) SYNTHESIS.md and TRANSLATION.md have no rule on how a garble-flagged extract item reaches brief content or renders (grep for garbl/extraction_note/FIDELITY in both returns only the rule-U note mention). The resulting defect is systematic: S3 garble normalised in 10/11 northlight briefs and 2/2 voreas (docs/EVAL_RECORD.md section 5; runs/tier3/KNOWN_DEFECTS.md B3; voreas Finding 1 already named it a spec gap on 2026-07-26). (2) Confidence semantics are overloaded and contradict each other. SOURCES.md:77 defines `low` as 'implied only', while rule G (:117, :133) and mandatories (:113) assign `low` to stated items. TRANSCRIPTS.md:22's annotation example says `confidence high`, the very phrase the extractor then sees inline. KNOWN_DEFECTS B4 (garbled items carried at high) is the observed outcome, and no gate checks it. (3) SYNTHESIS rule 6 (confidence never inflates) and the general form of rule 7 (conditional items stay conditional) have no deterministic check in check_synthesis; only the same-speaker retraction case is enforced. (4) The edited, decontaminated prompts have never been run by any model: every graded run predates the edits (EVAL_RECORD section 3 and section 7). (5) The render work order (stages.py build_render_order) restates about 10 TRANSLATION.md rules in its own words, against the extraction order's stated principle that orders 'never restate' the rules, which invites drift. render.md's wrapper also lacks the protected-path/hash-check sentence the other wrappers carry.
defects: No garble carry-through rule in SYNTHESIS.md or TRANSLATION.md; the garble is normalised silently in reader-visible content in 10/11 northlight and 2/2 voreas briefs (EVAL_RECORD section 5 S3, KNOWN_DEFECTS B3).

Confidence definitions contradict each other: SOURCES.md:77 says 'low = implied only', but rule G (:117) and mandatories (:113) assign low to stated items. TRANSCRIPTS.md:22's annotation example emits 'confidence high' inline. The observed result is B4, garbled items at high, and no gate catches it.

SYNTHESIS rule 6 (no confidence inflation) and the general form of rule 7 (qualifiers survive) are not machine-checked in pipeline/stages.py check_synthesis, so an instruction relies on model self-discipline despite the project's gate-over-prompt principle.
The decontaminated prompts (r1-W2) have zero live validation, so no evidence shows the rewritten examples still teach the rules.

build_render_order duplicates TRANSLATION.md rules in paraphrase, which gives two sources of truth for one stage. render.md's wrapper omits the protected-path sentence present in extract/fidelity/synthesize wrappers.
scores.to_reach_9: Add an explicit garble carry-through rule to SYNTHESIS.md and TRANSLATION.md, with a gate. Make confidence semantics single-valued (explicit overrides for rule G and mandatories; remove 'confidence high' from the fidelity annotation format or rename it), with a check_extract gate. Machine-check SYNTHESIS rules 6/7 in check_synthesis. Trim the render order to parameters only. Then show the decontaminated prompts green on the round-2 re-baseline, with S3/B4 xfails flipping to XPASS.

scores.evidence: Strengths verified: eval/cost_report.py defaults to tokens by model (fresh input, output, cache read, cache write). It counts every attempt, including repairs, failures and the per-source verify-extract (a separate 'verification' row via _stage_attempts), and de-duplicates resumed legs by session_id (running it over runs/ printed '35 attempt(s) copied into resumed runs were counted once'). It labels routing era from the models actually used (routing_era), and prints all-runs and clean-only means side by side. Dollars sit only behind --usd with explicit caveats. Resolved model IDs are captured per call from --output-format json (agents.py SubagentResult.model_ids; runs/tier3 shows claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 / claude-sonnet-5 / claude-opus-4-8). Effort policy lives in config/model_routing.json, and agents.stage_effort (agents.py:266) fails loudly on bad values. --risk-replay measured that 0/66 stored extracts take the base (haiku) verifier branch. docs/COST_MODEL.md, EVIDENCE.md and README.md:47 all carry an era banner, and COST_MODEL.md frames the value unit as an open owner decision (section 5). Weaknesses: (1) The routing adopted on 2026-07-30 is still unmeasured end to end on 2026-09-23. The only current-routing figure is one transcript leg (runs/routing-validate-01: 598,743 tokens, 2.0x the graded leg). So every published per-brief planning number (984,820; mean 848,845) describes a superseded routing. (2) That one leg shows 77% of its tokens (462,130; 20 turns) in the verifier-triggered repair. Yet no per-stage turn or token budget exists: grep for max-turns/max_turns/budget in pipeline/, eval/ and config/ is empty, and the only ceiling is a 1200 s timeout (agents.py:76). There is no anomaly threshold in the ruler either. (3) The risk-routed verifier is nominal. risk_classes (extraction.py:223) fires 'figures' on any digit, including dates, and 'garbling' on any extraction_note, including rule-U notes. The base branch is dead config, but CLAUDE.md and model_routing.json still describe 'else haiku' (logged as an open owner decision in EVAL_RECORD section 6, unresolved). (4) The per-brief means treat non-independent runs as samples: cost-c1b, cost-c2 and cost-c3 share the same classification/fidelity/extraction/synthesis sessions (verified in their manifests), so 'clean runs only n=7' is roughly 4 independent briefs, and COST_MODEL.md section 2 publishes it as a spread. (5) render effort=low was calibrated against 'fresh harness 17/17' (model_routing.json _calibration_rule), a metric blind to Greek quality (EVAL_RECORD section 4). Meanwhile tier3 has 9 Greek grammar errors (KNOWN_DEFECTS R3). (6) extraction._verify_policy (extraction.py:214) silently falls back to defaults on malformed config, the opposite of stage_effort's documented fail-loud rationale. (7) Verified-repair attempts are booked under 'extraction' (run_gated stage='extraction'), so the ruler cannot show what the verifier loop costs, which is the largest driver in the one current-routing measurement. docs/AUDIT_BRIEF.md:112 still quotes '~$2.25, 6 model calls' for an end-to-end run.
defects: The current routing (2026-07-30) is unmeasured end to end. All per-brief token figures (COST_MODEL.md sections 1-2, README.md:47, EVIDENCE.md) describe the superseded Haiku-era routing, and the one current leg is 2.0x the old one.
No per-stage turn/token budget or anomaly alert exists, although the only current-routing measurement shows a single verified-repair call at 462,130 tokens / 20 turns (77% of the leg).

The verify-extract risk routing is nominal: base branch 0/66 (risk_classes treats any digit as 'figures' and any note as 'garbling'). CLAUDE.md and model_routing.json still describe a haiku path that never runs.

The per-brief means count runs that share inherited legs (cost-c1b/c2/c3 reuse the same four model sessions) as independent samples, inflating n and skewing the 'clean mean' in COST_MODEL.md section 2.
render effort=low was validated only against the 17/17 harness, which cannot see Greek grammar, the dimension most likely to degrade at lower effort.
_verify_policy silently falls back on malformed model_routing.json, inconsistent with stage_effort's fail-loud rule for the same file.
Verified-repair tokens are booked as 'extraction', hiding the verifier loop's cost. docs/AUDIT_BRIEF.md:112 is stale ('~$2.25, 6 model calls').
scores.to_reach_9: Run the authorised 3-roll x 2-fixture re-baseline under current routing and republish per-brief tokens by model, with n over independent briefs. Add per-stage max-turns/token budgets in config/model_routing.json, enforced via the CLI and flagged by cost_report. Label verified-repair as its own stage. Get the owner to either redefine the risk classes (with a replay showing a real base-branch share) or collapse to 'always sonnet'. Recalibrate render effort against Greek lint and the supplementary checks, not only the harness. Make _verify_policy fail loudly.

scores.evidence: Strengths verified: eval/harness.py was frozen at Tier 1 before the artifacts it grades existed, and its one post-freeze commit (path plumbing) is disclosed (EVAL_RECORD section 4). The answer key is unreachable by construction: gates.HARNESS_ONLY_FILES, staged inputs, and an agents.permission_rules deny on //**/answer_key.json. eval/grade_frozen.py grades committed evidence read-only, with a before/after fingerprint. eval/pass_rates.py computes per-check pass rates over distinct legs, with Wilson 95% intervals. eval/supplementary.py adds nine report-only checks for named harness blind spots (X2 absence-pass, T3.3 anchor-grep, T2.5 glossary source, X3 literal patterns). Known output defects are pinned as 48 strict xfails that flip on a fix (the suite ran 948 passed, 7 skipped, 48 xfailed). tests/test_prompt_hygiene.py guards against re-contamination. The round-2 re-baseline protocol is pre-registered, with no re-roll-to-pass, and n=3 limits stated (EVAL_RECORD section 7). The docs keep deterministic proof and model-quality evidence apart unusually well (eval/agency_benchmark.py's docstring and not_measured list). Weaknesses: (1) No graded evidence exists for the configuration actually shipped. All 15 harness reports are Haiku-era, with contaminated prompts (EVAL_RECORD sections 1 and 3); sonnet extraction plus verifier and the decontaminated prompts have zero graded runs. (2) Fixture base: only 2 keyed fixtures (northlight_01, voreas_02), both synthetic and from the same author. voreas is no longer held out: its defects shaped SOURCES.md section 5, the gates and the xfails (EVAL_RECORD section 3), and no replacement held-out fixture was created. The three agency_* fixtures have no answer key and have never had a model run (EVAL_RECORD section 2; `ls fixtures/agency_*` shows only rfp.md, email.md, glossary.json, data_declaration.json). (3) Variance is thin. Northlight has 9-10 distinct legs per check, several of them resumed legs of each other, and voreas has 1-2 (Wilson 0.34-1.00). Re-roll outcomes graded into the same directory were overwritten and lost. The headline graded run runs/tier3 is itself assembled from resumed legs with a repair, and the 29 July capture needed a disclosed re-roll after X1 slipped. (4) The harness measures recall only, through keyword and signal matching (T3.1 signal substrings, T3.2 keyword_any_of, X3 literal patterns). It has no precision metric (false conflicts, invented or misfiled entries) and no recall check for ordinary non-trap facts. Greek and creative quality rest on heuristics and lints, with no rubric-based human or LLM-judge scoring and no inter-rater protocol. (5) 'agency_benchmark' is 13 hand-built dict fixtures (eval/agency_benchmark.py run()): a unit-level fault-injection check, not a benchmark. (6) EVAL_RECORD section 3 is stale at HEAD. It still says 'W2 is removing' the fixture quotes and cites line ranges (e.g. SOURCES.md:136-151) that now hold the decontaminated example, so the contamination status of the current prompts is misdescribed.
defects: Zero harness-graded runs under the current routing or the decontaminated prompts; all quality evidence is for a superseded configuration.
Only two keyed fixtures, both from the same author; the second (voreas_02) is no longer held out and no new held-out fixture replaced it. The agency_* fixtures have no answer keys and no model runs.
Variance evidence is thin and partly non-independent (resumed legs; voreas n=1-2). Re-roll outcomes were overwritten, and the headline run is an assembled, repaired run.
The harness is recall-only keyword matching, with no precision or false-conflict metric and no non-trap fact recall. Language and creative quality lack any rubric-based scoring.
eval/agency_benchmark.py is 13 synthetic unit cases labelled a benchmark.
docs/EVAL_RECORD.md section 3 describes decontamination as in progress, with line refs that no longer match HEAD.
scores.to_reach_9: Execute the pre-registered round-2 re-baseline (3 rolls x 2 fixtures, current routing, decontaminated prompts) and publish the per-check rates. Author a third keyed fixture blind (a separate session with no access to skills/gates), commit its answer key hash before the first run, and keep it held out. Write answer keys for the agency_* fixtures as new files. Add unfrozen precision/fact-recall scoring and a small rubric-based bilingual review (two raters, agreement reported). Update EVAL_RECORD section 3 to the post-W2 state.

moves.title: Garble carry-through rule in SYNTHESIS/TRANSLATION plus a synthesis/render gate
moves.rationale: S3 (garble silently normalised where readers look) is systematic: 10/11 northlight and 2/2 voreas briefs, KNOWN_DEFECTS B3, and it has been a named spec gap since voreas Finding 1. Neither downstream skill says what to do with a rule-G item, and the frozen T3.3 passes because it greps anchors. This is the highest-yield single fix to the instruction set.
moves.concrete_changes: skills/SYNTHESIS.md: add rule 10: 'An extract item carrying a rule-G extraction_note keeps the source token in content, in «guillemets», followed by the note's proposal marked unconfirmed (e.g. «μπραντ αγουέρνες» [ASR — likely "brand awareness", unconfirmed]); confidence low; the item raises or links an open question.' Add the matching self-check item. skills/TRANSLATION.md: add a rule that such entries render the token plus the ASR flag in both languages. Re-sync the injected blocks in .claude/agents/synthesize.md and render.md (tests/test_agents.py enforces byte-equality). pipeline/stages.py: in check_synthesis, for every extract item with a rule-G note, require the entry citing its anchor to contain the corrupted token in content. In check_render, require the token in both renders. Port the logic from eval/supplementary.py check_garble_visibility. Expect the B3 xfails in tests/test_regression_northlight.py to be re-evaluated at the next live run.

moves.title: Make confidence and qualifier semantics single-valued and enforced
moves.rationale: SOURCES.md:77 ('low = implied only') conflicts with rule G and mandatories, and TRANSCRIPTS.md:22 shows 'confidence high' inline, where the extractor reads it. B4 (garbled items at high) follows. SYNTHESIS rules 6 and 7 are instructions without gates, contrary to the project's own gate-over-prompt design.
moves.concrete_changes: skills/SOURCES.md section 4 confidence block: add 'Overrides: a rule-G item is low whatever its wording; a mandatory over-extracted under section 6 is low.' skills/TRANSCRIPTS.md section 3: change the annotation format to `[FIDELITY: glossary-match "…", match strong|weak]` and update FIDELITY_ANNOTATION_RE only if needed; the existing regex already strips any [FIDELITY: …]. Re-sync the agents. pipeline/extraction.py check_extract: flag any item whose value contains a token named in an extraction_note or fidelity annotation while its confidence is not low. pipeline/stages.py check_synthesis: map each entry's evidence anchors to extract items. Flag an entry whose confidence exceeds its strongest supporting item's (rule 6), and flag an entry that is not conditional when all its supporting items are conditional (rule 7). Add negative tests in tests/test_stages.py and tests/test_extraction.py.

moves.title: Run the authorised round-2 re-baseline and republish era-current numbers
moves.rationale: Every quality and usage figure describes a superseded routing with contaminated prompts. The owner has already authorised the protocol (OPERATING_DECISIONS 2026-09-22, decision 1; EVAL_RECORD section 7), and decontamination has merged. This single action closes the largest defect in all three Layer-2 aspects.
moves.concrete_changes: After moves 1-2 merge (or explicitly before, labelled as such), run EVAL_RECORD section 7 exactly: 3 independent rolls each of northlight_01 and voreas_02 into runs/rebaseline-r2, then the harness, supplementary, pass_rates, cost_report and --risk-replay. Write runs/rebaseline_r2_report.md with per-check pass/n (Wilson), supplementary flag counts, tokens by model per brief (independent briefs only) and resolved model IDs. Update docs/COST_MODEL.md sections 1-3, docs/EVIDENCE.md, README.md:47-64 and START_HERE.html:196 to lead with current-routing figures, keeping Haiku-era as history. Add the .gitignore exception so the six roll directories are committed evidence.

moves.title: Per-stage turn/token budgets and a separate verified-repair ledger row
moves.rationale: The one current-routing measurement shows a single verifier-triggered repair consuming 462k tokens over 20 turns, yet the only guardrail is a 1200 s timeout. On a subscription window, runaway calls are the usage risk that matters, and the ruler currently hides the verifier loop's cost inside 'extraction'.
moves.concrete_changes: config/model_routing.json: add "budgets": {"extract": {"max_turns": N}, "verify-extract": {...}, "synthesize": {...}, "render": {...}}, with N set from measured p95 turns plus margin and provenance noted. pipeline/agents.py build_command: pass --max-turns from that block, validated with fail-loud semantics like stage_effort. pipeline/extraction.py: call run_gated with stage='verified_repair' for the post-verification repair. eval/cost_report.py: add VERIFIED_REPAIR to STAGE1, plus a --budget flag that lists any attempt whose total tokens exceed a per-stage threshold from config. Tests in tests/test_effort.py and tests/test_cost_report.py.

moves.title: Resolve the nominal verify-extract risk routing with a replayed option set
moves.rationale: 0/66 extracts take the base branch, because 'figures' matches any digit (dates included) and 'garbling' matches any extraction_note (rule-U notes included). The documented 'else haiku' path is dead config. Routing is the owner's call, but the owner needs a replayed alternative, not just the observation.
moves.concrete_changes: Implement candidate classifiers behind a flag in eval/cost_report.py --risk-replay: (a) figures = currency or amount patterns only, excluding dates and timestamps; garbling = notes matching the rule-G form only. (b) Always strong. Print the base-branch share for each over the stored extracts and the re-baseline extracts. Present the options in docs/EVAL_RECORD.md section 6. On the owner's decision, either narrow pipeline/extraction.py risk_classes accordingly, or set base_model to "sonnet" and remove the 'else haiku' wording from config/model_routing.json and CLAUDE.md's routing line. Also make extraction._verify_policy raise on malformed JSON, mirroring agents.stage_effort.

moves.title: Third keyed, blind-authored held-out fixture plus answer keys for the agency fixtures
moves.rationale: Two same-author fixtures, one of them no longer held out, cannot support any generalisation claim. The agency_* fixtures sit unused by any model evaluation.
moves.concrete_changes: Create fixtures/<new>_03/ (synthetic, new client and industry, 4-6 sources, seeded conflicts, gaps, garbles and X-traps), authored in a separate session with no read access to skills/, pipeline/ or tests/. Commit its answer_key.json with a SHA-256 recorded in docs/EVAL_RECORD.md before any pipeline run, and exclude it from any prompt or gate tuning (add its strings to tests/test_prompt_hygiene.py SEEDED_STRINGS). Add new answer_key.json files for fixtures/agency_paid_01, agency_organic_01 and agency_production_01; these are new files, so no existing key is edited. Grade the new fixtures once in the round-2 re-baseline as held-out rows, reported separately.

moves.title: Unfrozen precision, fact-recall and bilingual-rubric scoring
moves.rationale: The frozen harness is recall-only keyword matching. Precision (false conflicts, invented or misfiled entries), ordinary-fact recall and Greek quality are unmeasured, yet they are the defects the review panels actually found (KNOWN_DEFECTS B5, B6, B8, R3, R6).
moves.concrete_changes: eval/supplementary.py: add S10 fact_recall. Every extract item with confidence high must reach an entry, conflict or open question by anchor (reusing pipeline/quality.coverage). Add S11 conflict_precision: each brief conflict must have positions whose anchors come from items with differing values in the same field. Add eval/bilingual_rubric.md plus eval/rubric_score.py: a 6-item rubric (fidelity, register, grammar, terminology, hedge width, equivalence) scored by two raters, either human or a sonnet judge with a fixed prompt kept outside the pipeline's runtime prompts. Report Cohen's kappa. Record results beside the harness in runs/rebaseline_r2_report.md. Report-only; none of it becomes a gate without owner approval.

moves.title: Fix per-brief sample independence in the ruler and stale evaluation/usage docs
moves.rationale: COST_MODEL.md section 2's 'clean n=7' counts cost-c1b/c2/c3, which share four model sessions, as separate briefs. EVAL_RECORD section 3 still describes decontamination as pending, with dead line refs. AUDIT_BRIEF.md:112 quotes '~$2.25, 6 model calls' and instructs running the harness CLI on runs/tier3, which rewrites committed evidence.
moves.concrete_changes: eval/cost_report.py complete_briefs/brief_means: key each brief by the tuple of its model-leg session IDs, and compute means over distinct tuples. Alternatively, report 'independent briefs' (no inherited legs) as a third selection. Print n_independent. Update docs/COST_MODEL.md section 2 from the new output. docs/EVAL_RECORD.md section 3: rewrite in the past tense, record the W2 merge commit, and state that tests/test_prompt_hygiene.py now guards the prompts. docs/AUDIT_BRIEF.md: replace the cost line with a tokens-by-model pointer to COST_MODEL.md, and replace `python eval/harness.py runs/tier3` with `python3 eval/grade_frozen.py`. Add tests in tests/test_cost_report.py for the shared-leg case.

overall: Layer 2 is unusually disciplined and unusually candid for an MVP demo. The runtime instructions are precise, injected byte-exact and wrapped in CLI-enforced least privilege. Most rules have a deterministic gate that cites them. Usage is measured in tokens by model across every attempt, with era labels. The evaluation record states plainly what 17/17 does not prove. What keeps every aspect below 8 is one gap seen from three sides: the configuration that ships (sonnet extraction, risk-routed verifier, decontaminated prompts) has no graded run and no whole-brief usage measurement, and the routing change is eight weeks old. On top of that, concrete defects remain. The skills have no garble carry-through rule, although the resulting normalisation is systematic across both fixtures. Confidence semantics contradict each other. The verifier's risk routing is dead config. No per-stage budget guards against the 462k-token repair already observed. The evaluation rests on two same-author fixtures, one no longer held out, and recall-only keyword checks. Executing the already-authorised re-baseline after the two prompt/gate fixes would move all three aspects the most per unit of effort.
